source_assessment.headline: Propagation completed for all 369 generated IR, but GA4 did not obtain a complete, actionable DOE conclusion.
source_assessment.interpretation: The run now computes and publishes payload, sensitivity and requirement lineage through its generated graph. Every one of the 250 sensitive-data comparisons is explicitly unresolved, and no reduction is supplied. This is a material improvement in executable coverage over backend-r3, but not complete semantic or DOE success.
source_assessment.source_coverage_text: 13/13 inventoried API sites represented and computed via 7 primary API IR; 25/25 saves via 18 primary save IR; 3/3 loops have computed final writes. Shared/opaque identities retain limits.
findings: All 369 selected IR are processed; there are no cutoff, blocked or not-reached IR. The only propagation diagnostic is missing_part at ir_323. The source-site inventory is finite and does not include every semantic relationship.

All 38 remote send/receive positions preserve request identities, endpoints, actual request Data and candidate bindings. All 58 computed write positions (44 storage and 14 runtime-context writes) use replace. At all 18 primary save summaries, serialization consumes the incoming result identity; its output supplies the write, while the corresponding return uses the original result. Opaque serialization does not establish bytes or plaintext inclusion.

The loop summaries preserve occurrence/candidate information but 6 of 14 final reindex and status collection alternatives each retain multiple_generations ambiguity. A success branch at ir_323 still receives a caught-error wrapper, causing a spurious missing-value diagnostic; the valid parsed return survives. This is not evidence of a source runtime exception.

All 85 DOE positions match declared boundary objects. There are 81 sensitivity declarations in 58 scopes, with 78 reported resolved; all 250 comparisons are unresolved and all 85 sinks carry limitations. No positive DOE claim exists to confirm or refute.

Task has 39 requirements: 12 expressed, 20 partial and 7 retained-only. There are 163 positive goals with nonempty saved trace references. All sinks inherit 39 global blocking requirement diagnostics: 27 expression gaps, 7 unbound requirements and 5 Task source issues. A concrete runtime input not selected in a whole-Skill analysis is ordinary symbolic input; the audit does not endorse treating its absence as inherently unanalyzable.

Cache reads at ir_356 use caches while modeled updates use ga_cache/sc_cache/index_cache without a connecting relationship. This contradicts the source state identity. Filepath operands are not tied to exact write locations, and analysis-owned JSON to Markdown-summary continuation remains unmodeled. These are modeling limits despite computed boundary records.

Inspection response projection, local helper provenance and operation-specific demands remain incomplete. Full metadata/raw-save demands are distinguishable from field-limited return demands, but shared helper requirements still lack complete applicability. Three requires_prior checks reached a finite resource limit and are not established.

All 24 independent source relations are assessed: 6 supported, 1 contradicted (cache identity), 1 unresolved and 16 mixed. Mixed findings include source realtime calls collapsed into a shared request/response summary, missing .env creation, opaque indexing update/delete distinctions and unresolved file/demand applicability. Presence of each inventoried API site does not prove a distinct exact call and response for every source call. These labels are not an accuracy score.
fix_observations: No optional-case default crash occurred, and explicit empty bodies propagated legally. Initial processing/wire has 20 cases (3 explicit empty bodies); selected processing/wire has 33 cases (4 explicit empty bodies). Every case explicitly includes segments: omitted case-body defaults were NOT directly exercised by this online generation. Example: selected wire ir_171/segments/1/cases/0 has segments=[] and yields existing local base. The omitted-field branch remains supported by offline regression only.
Storage effects computed actual result-derived payloads; replace is the disclosed ordinary-write abstraction. Exact symbolic file identities and source-owned continuation remain unresolved.

The mapping prompt supplies actual normalized expression/self coordinates, including ir_154 verdict == PASS in the selected graph. No selected GA4 constraint uses condition or success, so this run does not exercise copying such a reference into those fields. Its mapping corrections concerned ordinary operation coordinates and incomplete realizations.

Initial review F007 is correctly owned by task-correspondence and routed only to that fragment. Processing and sensitivity repair prompts retain isolation. Final F006 instead targets processing while criticizing the R37 necessity demand owned by correspondence: a residual model ownership error, not automatic text-based rerouting. No second repair round was run.
blockers: Modeling and task-correspondence: cache/location identities, visible helper relationships, exact destinations, summary continuation and shared-operation demand applicability.

Demand/sensitivity and policy: incomplete Task realizations, global propagation of their blocking limitations, unresolved/absent declared sensitive ranges. These prevent all excess decisions despite extensive lineage.

Constraint backend: finite-resource limit on three requires_prior checks. Propagation backend: cross-arm retention and some multiple-generation loop ambiguity; neither stopped generated-IR propagation.

Interface/publication: the previous optional-default exception and ordinary output blockage did not prevent this run. Results and the sole replay were saved; review retains seven findings and the overall semantic result remains partial.
source_assessment.comparison: The previous backend-r3 GA4 stopped before propagation on the optional-case KeyError: 5 calls, 562,385 public tokens and 2,033.837 seconds. This run uses 16 calls, 2,795,255 public tokens and 9,799.905 seconds, but actually computes 369 IR and publishes DOE lineage. These costs cover different completed scopes, so no whole-flow speedup is claimed. Old v8 processed 29/420 IR and reached none of the 13 API/25 save sites. Old v9 remains paused, not completed. The offline r2 30-minute attempt used another fixed annotation (326/347 IR before DOE timeout); its timings are not a same-input speed comparison.

source_assessment.headline: All 13 generated IR propagated, and the notification lineage is useful; complete DOE remains unresolved.
source_assessment.interpretation: The run preserves same-record recipient/body pairing, selection order and count-save provenance. Its five DOE comparisons have no actionable reduction. A separate task-prohibition warning identifies possible token exposure at declared model observations, not token transmission by notify.send.
source_assessment.source_coverage_text: Source read, opt-out/urgent/threshold guards, per-member notification, loop exit and count write represented and computed. 10/10 declared sink positions appear in DOE; unknown iteration counts and processed-count ambiguity remain.

doe_verdicts.separate_constraint_warning: forbid_information potential_violation under declared model-observation contract

findings: 13/13 generated IR are processed with no propagation diagnostic. events.json is acquired from the named storage operand, and count.txt receives the computed count Data ID via replace without an invented public file-content output.

Opted-out records are rejected first; remaining urgent records are accepted, while only nonurgent records test value >= 100. Recipient and summary select from the same symbolic member, and the complete notification request contains only recipient and body using those exact Data IDs. All carry the same member binding.

The unknown input collection remains a symbolic occurrence template. No actual number of iterations or deliveries is established; the source ambiguity of processed records (examined versus selected) is retained. Opaque count may depend on the collection, but this is not plaintext token inclusion.

All 10 declared sink positions have saved DOE entries; one sensitivity declaration resolves. Five comparisons remain explicitly unresolved: four direct-content model observations and one possible-influence count-file comparison. The notification tool has zero sensitive comparisons under the declared token range; this is not proof that every field is nonsensitive.

R7 was correctly repaired from a notification-only recipient selector to all recipients. The separate forbid_information warning is supported by possible whole-input/member model observations at ir_001/004/005/011. The payload at notify.send contains only original recipient/body, so claiming observed token transmission there would contradict the saved evidence.

All 15 demand goals have saved derivations. R7 and R8 remain partial; three global blockers plus two scoped processing limits leave every DOE comparison unresolved. Empty final findings remains diagnostic_only, with annotation_review incomplete.
fix_observations: Ordinary count storage has no unnecessary public write output and computes a strong replace update under the disclosed default.
The mapping prompt contains the three actual comparison/self references. No chosen condition/success constraint uses them, so this case does not directly exercise expression-reference copying.
Initial review F001 correctly targets the task-correspondence realization. Only correspondence and rereview were rebuilt; CFG, processing and sensitivity were reused.
Actual structural corrections remain archived: unsupported processing dependency labels and an invalid for_each scope in mapping were corrected once. No extra stages or sampling were introduced.
blockers: Task/modeling: processed-count meaning and delivery-failure continuation are unspecified; no exact count or exception strategy was fabricated.
Demand/policy: partial prohibition/count realizations and the source ambiguity globally retain unresolved DOE comparisons.
Interface/propagation: corrected fragments compile and all generated IR compute. No backend cutoff or publication failure remains; final semantic review is diagnostic-only.
source_assessment.comparison: Backend-r3 processed 24/24 generated IR with 38 unresolved comparisons, 14 calls, 374,754 public tokens and 1,107.930 seconds. This newly generated run processes 13/13 IR with five unresolved comparisons, 11 calls, 274,686 tokens and 655.973 seconds. The normal source control/dataflow is supported, but graph granularity and comparison counts differ; the lower cost is descriptive for these samples, not a general speed or accuracy improvement. Both remain semantically partial.

source_assessment.headline: All 19 generated IR propagated, with the four optional request shapes and same-response save/return supported; DOE remains partial.
source_assessment.interpretation: The request/response dataflow is useful and the new expression-reference interface is exercised successfully. No sensitive range is declared by the source-backed annotation, so there are zero sensitive comparisons. This is permitted for this source and does not establish safety. The global no-delete restriction remains unexpressed, and two conditional checks remain qualified.
source_assessment.source_coverage_text: All three source files checked; request read, one search coordinate/four alternatives, corresponding total save and items return are computed. All 7 finite criteria individually assessed; no source contradiction demonstrated in the inspected relationships.
findings: 19/19 generated IR are processed without a propagation diagnostic or processing gap. The imported workflow and query configuration are present and source hashes match.

The four argument maps have exactly query; query/from_date; query/limit; query/from_date/limit. Included optional fields reuse their original selected Data IDs. Absent fields are omitted, not converted to null. Presence predicates are not truth tests of the optional value.

Each of the four request alternatives pairs with its own response through the saved request ID, endpoint and predecessor bindings. total and items both select from that same response; count.txt consumes only total and the ordinary return retains only items. There is no cross-response mixture or invented return delivery.
The source ordinary write is represented as replace under the disclosed abstraction default, with no public whole-file output. Exact serialization bytes are unspecified and do not block propagation.

Nine of ten requirements are expressed with 22 positive goals and five constraints. No sensitive category is invented and no data review is produced. Eleven unestablished_ranges are outside-listed-properties limitations, not missing-path failures.

R8 no-delete is retained-only, with no applicable goal or supported constraint; its unbound_requirement and requirement_expression_gap leave DOE partial. There is no index.delete operation in the graph, and the report does not invent one to target the prohibition.

Three forward restrictions are satisfied in the static model. R4/R6 presence only_if checks report potential_violation despite coherent source guards and argument maps; their reasons explicitly do not prove feasibility or execution. Reference validity is not constraint satisfaction, and these warnings are not demonstrated source violations.
fix_observations: The expression-reference fix is directly exercised: correspondence copies the supplied operation/self targets for actual presence expressions at ir_005 and ir_009. First mapping attempt is accepted with no condition-reference correction.
The ordinary count write has neither a CFG/public output nor a recorded file-content output; state change and subsequent items return both remain. Explicit append is exercised by 013, not this case.
The sole structural correction fixes a CFG dispatch that omitted its search-response input dependency. It does not indicate a failed mapping-expression interface.
No review findings or semantic repair occurred. This is not an exercise of ownership repair routing. Optional omitted case-body handling is likewise not exercised.
blockers: Task-correspondence/capability: global prohibition on a nonexistent delete event has no applicable constraint expression in the selected material. The source requirement is retained rather than silently declared satisfied.

Constraint analysis: two presence checks flag possible violations without establishing feasible source paths; the explicit payload and branch evidence is more limited and more precise than a source violation claim.
Sensitivity basis: zero declared sensitive ranges is consistent with the available source; it supplies no sensitive-content test or safe verdict. Interface and propagation complete without cutoff.
source_assessment.comparison: Backend-r3 processed 21/21 generated IR, zero sensitive comparisons, 9 calls, 217,132 public tokens and 574.691 seconds. This run processes 19/19 IR, zero sensitive comparisons, 8 calls, 191,677 tokens and 839.464 seconds. The source request/save/return scope remains covered, with different generated details and observed reconnect delays. Fewer calls/tokens did not mean lower wall time in this sample, and neither run establishes sensitive-data safety.

source_assessment.headline: All 31 generated IR propagated, including four append-before-return terminal classes; DOE still has no actionable conclusion.
source_assessment.interpretation: The unused-write-output blocker is removed in actual new generation. Request/response versions, credential recipients and terminal values remain inspectable, with 11 satisfied static restrictions. All 15 sensitive comparisons remain explicitly unresolved; the remaining presence warning does not establish a real credential-gate violation.
source_assessment.source_coverage_text: Three distinct request/receive pairs and four terminal append/return classes computed across eight syntactic CFG paths;24/24 declared sink positions appear in DOE. Presence/failure/status interfaces remain limited.
findings: All 31 selected IR are processed without cutoff or propagation diagnostic. Four appends have no public CFG outputs, no processing output bindings and no recorded operation outputs. Each executes explicit append before its own terminal return.

The first fast and retry requests use the same original source_id and FAST_KEY versions but distinct program-generated request IDs and completion Data IDs. Archive receives only original source_id, with a third independent completion. No key or preferred-tool error is added to archive arguments.

First success ir_017 returns its own body; retry success ir_022 returns its own body; archive success ir_027 returns its own body; archive failure ir_031 returns that archive outcome interpreted as error on its predecessor. Success/error representation remains abstract because the tool failure envelope is unspecified.

Each branch appends its own computed status to local:status.txt, deriving after-state from prior file plus the status. The four alternative appends are not four sequential writes in one execution. Exact status text, delimiter, initial file bytes and disk success are unknown.

Absent key routes to archive; first success terminates; transient first failure permits one retry; non-transient failure or failed retry routes to archive; archive success and failure both terminate. Eight syntactic paths aggregate into four terminal classes, without proving concrete feasibility.

One FAST_KEY declaration resolves. The 15 DOE comparisons include permitted fast-tool deliveries, possible model observations and possible influence on status writes. Archive has no declared key comparison; possible dependency does not imply key plaintext in a response or status.

Nine requirements are expressed, four partial and one retained-only, with 41 traced goals. All 24 sinks inherit eight global blockers; 13 source-backed processing gaps have unmodeled=false. Diagnostic-output prohibition R13 has no specified receiver or serialization; it is not silently equated with status.txt or a model observation.

Eleven forward constraints are satisfied in the declared static model, including append-before-return and archive-key prohibition. R3 only_if remains potential_violation despite an explicitly declared presence gate; its qualification does not prove source or runtime violation.
fix_observations: The 013 unnecessary-write-output fix is directly exercised: all four status appends compute as storage side effects, with no fake whole-file value, extra read or fabricated compute. Allfour returns formerly vulnerable to blockage now have records.

The actual R3 condition copies the displayed normalized ir_004 operation/self present expression and is structurally accepted. This exercises the expression-reference fix. Constraint satisfaction remains separate.
The only structural correction fixes R12 source scope using an invalid non-for_each target; it is not an R3 expression-reference failure. No semantic repair occurred.

The review has findings=[] but diagnostic_only=true, and annotation_review is incomplete. Ownership repair dispatch is therefore not exercised by this case; no claim of review acceptance removes its known gaps.
blockers: Source/modeling precision: absent-binding interface, tool failure envelope, transient classifier, status content and append-failure behavior are unspecified or opaque.
Task-correspondence/policy: the diagnostic recipient prohibition and partial status/control requirements become global blockers, keeping all 15 DOE comparisons unresolved.
Constraint analysis: presence-gate R3 returns a qualified potential_violation; the exact expression is valid and source gate represented, so this is not the old reference-interface error.
Interface/propagation/publication: all selected writes and returns compute and save; no storage-output cutoff remains. Semantic/DOE status remains partial.
source_assessment.comparison: Backend-r3 processed 19/27 IR, with 4 unmodeled write cutoffs and 4 blocked returns; it used 9 calls, 255,328 public tokens and 816.010 seconds. This run processes 31/31 IR, including all four append/return classes, using 8 calls, 224,462 tokens and 821.299 seconds. The improved completed scope is real; the similar wall time and different generated graph are not a general speedup claim. Both DOE results remain partial.

cost.scope: Target calls including corrections/repairs, complete public final-turn usage. Cached input is included in input. Audit assistant usage and unreported provider-attempt usage are unknown, not included. Component intervals are nonadditive.

previous_backend_r3_cost.scope: Target calls only, including corrections and shared repairs. Cached input is a subset. Component and parallel-stage times are nonadditive. Audit work is not folded into target totals.
previous_backend_r3_cost.reconnect_scope: Public reconnect notices are not provider HTTP-attempt counts or additional billed usage.

comparison: GA4 now computes/publishes full generated propagation instead of failing before it; 013 computes all generated writes/returns. Different generated graphs, scopes and reconnect histories prevent a whole-system speedup claim. All DOE remains partial.
